• Develop training material, including:
    • participant guides,
    • job aids,
    • quick reference material,
    • e-learning,
    • instructor guides,
    • case studies, and
    • pre-reading material.
  • Design and develop the training feedback and assessment mechanisms to be used in order to evaluate the effectiveness of the training courses.

• EY involvement in development of training varies from one project to the next and the role (i.e., client advisor vs. system integrator) EY plays on the project is a major factor
  • In general terms, development of training content and material should focus on providing context for participants to understand why a new platform, solution or system is being used
  • The EY role on the engagement will determine the involvement in developing the training material, but generally this should focus on contextualising the training so participants understand why they are doing things differently, using a new system etc.

Where procedures have been updated, the basis for the training should be those updated procedures.

In many cases, training content may be developed off shore or third party vendor. It is critical to check the training material not just for accuracy and quality, but also to assess adherence to the training design principles set in earlier phases.

In addition, training content must be reviewed not only for basics, such as the screenshots matching the new system, but also to ensure that the integrity of the training content is maintained and complete. This means that training content addresses both system and process elements.

To define learning content that helps train end users on what they need to effectively perform their role, and to make sure those materials conform to the applicable standards and mee stakeholder expectations.
